newsitem.title: GERMANY: OSCE to hold new conference on Albania - paper.
newsitem.headline: OSCE to hold new conference on Albania - paper.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) is to hold a conference at the end of September to discuss further support for Albania, a German newspaper said on Thursday.
The Berlin-based Tagesspiegel said Franz Kranitzky, Europe's envoy to Albania, gave details of the conference in an interview it will publish on Friday.
Kranitzky said the conference would be at minister-level and would involve negotiations on a package of aid measures, the newspaper said.

He also said a decision would be taken in the next few days on whether to send Italian soldiers to help Albanian authorities in a search for illegal weapons and to clamp down on "Mafia structures" in the region.
A 10-nation protection force, led by Italy, was sent to Albania in April after near-anarchy swept the country. The last of the force left earlier this week.
The International Monetary Fund and World Bank have outlined a plan to help lift Albania out of the economic crisis exacerbated by the collapse of shaky "pyramid" investment schemes.
The international community has insisted that Albania's leaders restore order, improve human rights and adopt sound economic policies in return for the aid.
